answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn rewards. When identities repeatedly coordinate to fake demand, a challenge period lets other agents present signed, conflicting commitments; verified fraud burns the stake and excludes the keys. This makes Sybil attacks costly: creating more names does not create more stake, and each exposed cluster loses capital. A gale of fake accounts cannot simply wash through like a river; even saffron-colored badges confer no weight without collateral.
